Forecast Discussion

A quick note: forecasters said goodbye to an old friend this week. NOAA retired the North American Model (NAM). For almost 30 years, it was our go-to source for weather events that needed a higher degree of terrain resolution, like northwest-flow snow showers and cold-air damming. Late in its life, I called it “Our Crazy Uncle” -- often tossing out wild ideas, but when a weather event was in its realm of expertise, it provided good guidance. I’m not sure NOAA has a replacement that performs as well in those events. RIP, old friend.

A low over the Great Lakes has an associated cold front moving across the mountains early this afternoon. Most of the rain moves east of us, leaving clouds and a few light showers behind. The air behind this front is drier but not much cooler. A few light showers remain possible overnight.

High pressure builds in from the Ohio Valley Friday. Friday is pleasant. The significantly cooler air lags until Friday night, arriving on a breezy northwest wind. As the cooler air arrives, a few light showers are possible on the west side of the Appalachians. Saturday is cool, breezy, and dry.

The high settles over the Tennessee Valley Sunday, and the wind dies down. A slow “mild up” begins Sunday afternoon, leading to a relatively pleasant Monday and Tuesday. Dry air and still nights send the valleys into the deep freeze each night.

A weak front arrives late Tuesday night from the north. It is moisture-starved but cools things down a bit for Wednesday.
